newsitem.title: UK: Cornwall address raided in copper investigation.
newsitem.headline: Cornwall address raided in copper investigation.

text.p: An address in Cornwall (western England) was raided by police late last week as part of the ongoing investigation into the world copper market that followed the Sumitomo Corp scandal, the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said on Monday.
"On Friday, a search warrant was executed at an address in Rock, Cornwall, as part of the investigation into the affairs of Mr Hamanaka," an SFO spokeswoman said.
The SFO declined to say who the premises raided on Friday belonged to. The investigation is continuing, she said.
However, the Guardian newspaper said Monday that the home belonged to Charles Vincent, one of the co-founders of Winchester Commodities.

Winchester is a British metals brokerage founded in 1991 by Vincent and fellow Briton Ashley Levett. Winchester prospered by offering highly sophisticated metals brokering skills, and until 1995 numbered Sumitomo among its top clients.

Since the Sumitomo scandal erupted it has cut back on its activities, laid off staff, and is no longer acting as an introducing broker. Winchester has strongly denied any role in the losses and said it will co-operate with regulatory and fraud inquiries. Levett and Vincent are no longer directors, but remain shareholders.

Winchester spokesmen were not immediately available for comment on Monday. The SFO inquiry follows the disclosure on June 14 by Sumitomo that it had sacked its former head trader Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he ran up losses worth $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper deals.
In August, the SFO and City of London Police executed search warrants at two residential premises in Hampshire, Southern England as part of the enquiry.
British police raids also took place on homes and offices in the UK offshore tax haven of Guernsey in May.
